title: The Last Protocol Revisited
premise: Xenolinguist Isandro Eriksen, exiled to a failing research colony for refusing to weaponize an alien grammar, documents its abandonment until a nine-second gravity flicker reveals that the flicker was a handshake: a dormant alien network beneath the colony has been counting Earth's dying transmission loop as a countdown. The network offers to wake half the system's frozen colonists and let the other half's bodies feed its reawakening. Isandro, who now dreams only in the aliens' language, must choose which half of humanity survives, and by translating the network's own concept of debt, convinces it to accept testimony instead of flesh, waking everyone at the cost of the colony and the alien archive itself.
about_author: Silas Halloran is the pen name of a former field linguist who spent six years documenting endangered languages in the Arctic before turning to fiction. They write slow, grief-laced science fiction about people who keep records no one asked for.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The colony's last eleven residents eke out routines while Isandro records everything, including their own dreams, which have stopped being human. Then gravity stutters for nine seconds, and every machine on the planet answers with the same pulse. The emotional beat is dread braided with relief: after years of being forgotten, something finally noticed them, and that is not a comfort.

chapters.title: The Grammar Under the Ice
chapters.summary: Alternating Isandro and engineer Tovi Okonkwo. Following the pulse into the ice, they find the alien network and learn the flicker was a handshake: Earth's transmission loop is a countdown, and when it ends, the network wakes half the sleepers and consumes the rest. Isandro realizes they alone can read the network's intent. The beat is vertigo: fluency becomes power, and power arrives already corrupted.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, fracturing the colony. The survivors split over the choice: Tovi wants a lottery, administrator Vess wants to stack it with the young and useful, and Isandro secretly begins translating the network's concept of debt, discovering it was itself betrayed by its makers. The beat is moral collapse and regrouping, as found family argues like family does: viciously, lovingly, with the clock running.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the transmission loop's final cycle, Isandro offers the network a trade: instead of bodies, it will receive the colony's full recorded archive, every grief, every name, every dream in two languages, as evidence of what its makers destroyed and what humans are. The network accepts, wakes everyone, and dissolves, taking the colony with it. The beat is grief transmuted into justice: no law was served, but a debt was finally paid.
